SMTO-HTTP-0017 — The sign-in for the web service expired

GUID: e70ffcc0-d2fd-42c4-b380-0866502afc6a
Slug: http-oauth-expired
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO asked you to sign in to a web service, but the sign-in wasn't finished before its time ran out. SMTO didn't connect and didn't use the service with your account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to connect to the service again. Each sign-in link or device code works only once and for a limited time, so you need a new one.
  2. When the prompt appears, select Open authorization page and finish signing in within about 10 minutes. If a device code is shown, select Copy device code and enter it there. Finishing quickly keeps you inside the time limit for the new sign-in.
  3. Keep the SMTO page open and don't select Stop until the sign-in prompt disappears. Stop cancels the waiting sign-in, which would make you start over.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in prompt disappears and SMTO continues the task using the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never put passwords, device codes or access tokens in the conversation, screenshots or error reports.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth flow expired: the provider returned expired_token, or the authorization-code or device transaction passed its expiry before completion.

What this means

  • OAuth returned expired_token, or the authorization/device transaction exceeded its monotonic expiry. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth returned expired_token, or the authorization/device transaction exceeded its monotonic expiry.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the owned transaction type and expiry, keeping codes and tokens private.

How to fix it

  • OAuth2.accept maps an expired_token response to this error, and OAuth2.prepare_session raises it when an authorization-code callback arrives after the transaction's 600-second monotonic expiry or a device-code transaction passes its expiry (the provider's expires_in, default 600 s, capped at 1800 s). Discard the expired flow state and start a fresh authorization that the user completes before it expires.
  • Start a fresh authorization flow; discard expired flow state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh supported authorization transaction completes before expiration.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
